card.headline: It costs an arm and a leg!

beats.speech: And the idiom: It costs an arm and a leg!

language_approval.notes: All 5 beats read. ONE change: beat 1 pricey -> overpriced (speech + card headline): 'pricey' is only informal for 'expensive' (Oxford/Cambridge), not stronger. overpriced = too expensive, costing more than it is worth (Oxford); costly = very expensive / more than you want to pay (Longman, Oxford), 'costly repairs' standard collocation; exorbitant = much too high, 'exorbitant rent' standard. Nuance: all three say the price is too high, none is a neutral intensifier. 'cost an arm and a leg' is a current dictionary idiom. Subjects it/the repairs/the rent drawable with the boy mascot. No sentence shared with listen-100 ('It was a costly mistake.') or any other unit (grep). Card text = speech. caps OK.
